o1.biggest_strength: It turns the key signals into a usable plan: worker/on-feet Spark Ads from day 1, problem-first hooks, a $38 target tied to 90-day contribution, and a $30,000 budget that adds up.
o1.biggest_mistake: It is a little lighter on attribution hygiene and compliance details, such as excluding current buyers, paid-partnership disclosure, and checking TikTok against Shopify during the month.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add current-customer exclusion, paid creator disclosure, weekly Shopify-vs-TikTok reconciliation, and a slightly stronger two-read incrementality test for the day-30 decision.

o2.biggest_strength: It is very Monday-ready and operational, with the right worker-first creative, learning-phase budget logic, tracking gates, Spark Ads, rights planning, and a day-30 read that does not blindly trust TikTok ROAS.
o2.biggest_mistake: It invents or over-assumes a few items, especially the $95,000 paid-spend share/Meta-at-$65,000 assumption and the 'to confirm' section when the owner asked for assumptions, not follow-up questions.

reason: Both are strong and usable, but Output 2 is the one I would rather hand to the team because it has better learning-phase logic, tracking gates, creator-rights details, and a more realistic measurement plan. Output 1 is safer on assumptions, but Output 2 gives the media buyer more of the operating system needed for the first 30 days.
